title: FDA Drug Approvals Targeting GPCR Mechanisms, 2021 to 2026
summary: GPCR-targeted drugs the FDA approved from 2021 to mid-2026, with receptor targets, receptor classes, and therapeutic areas.
body_text: FDA drug approvals targeting GPCR mechanisms, 2021 to 2026 G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) remain the single most productive target family in small-molecule and peptide drug development, and the FDA's approval record since 2021 reflects that. Across Drugs@FDA, at least eighteen distinct products approved between 2021 and mid-2026 act primarily through a GPCR, spanning class B secretin-family receptors (the incretin and glucagon receptors), class A aminergic and peptide receptors, lipid-sensing receptors, and chemokine receptors. The therapeutic footprint is unusually broad: cardiometabolic disease, migraine, schizophrenia, insomnia, multiple sclerosis and ulcerative colitis, gynecology and menopause, ANCA-associated vasculitis, chronic-kidney-disease pruritus, hepatorenal syndrome, stem-cell mobilization in multiple myeloma, and opioid-overdose reversal. The clearest theme is the dominance of incretin biology. Beyond that, the period produced several genuine first-in-class GPCR agents, including the first muscarinic-agonist antipsychotic (Cobenfy), the first oral C5a-receptor antagonist (Tavneos), and the first neurokinin-3 receptor antagonist for menopausal vasomotor symptoms (Veozah). Snapshot of GPCR-targeted approvals since 2021 Product Active ingredient GPCR target (receptor class) Therapeutic area Original FDA approval Wegovy semaglutide GLP-1 receptor agonist (class B) Obesity / cardiometabolic Jun 2021 375 Mounjaro tirzepatide GIP + GLP-1 receptor agonist (class B) Type 2 diabetes May 2022 354 Zepbound tirzepatide GIP + GLP-1 receptor agonist (class B) Obesity / OSA Nov 2023 357 Foundayo orforglipron GLP-1 receptor agonist, oral (class B) Cardiometabolic Apr 2026 479 Zegalogue dasiglucagon Glucagon receptor agonist (class B) Severe hypoglycemia Mar 2021 435 Qulipta atogepant CGRP receptor antagonist (class B) Migraine prevention Sep 2021 225 Zavzpret zavegepant CGRP receptor antagonist (class B) Acute migraine Mar 2023 231 Cobenfy xanomeline / trospium M1/M4 muscarinic agonist (class A) Schizophrenia Sep 2024 36 Quviviq daridorexant Orexin OX1R/OX2R antagonist (class A) Insomnia Jan 2022 332 Ponvory ponesimod S1P receptor-1 modulator (class A) Relapsing MS Mar 2021 271 Velsipity etrasimod S1P receptor 1/4/5 modulator (class A) Ulcerative colitis Oct 2023 259 Myfembree relugolix (combination) GnRH receptor antagonist (class A) Fibroids / endometriosis May 2021 199 Veozah fezolinetant Neurokinin-3 (NK3) receptor antagonist (class A) Menopausal vasomotor symptoms May 2023 66 Korsuva difelikefalin Kappa opioid receptor agonist (class A) CKD-associated pruritus Aug 2021 90 Tavneos avacopan Complement C5a receptor antagonist (class A) ANCA-associated vasculitis Oct 2021 185 Terlivaz terlipressin Vasopressin V1a receptor agonist (class A) Hepatorenal syndrome Sep 2022 75 Aphexda motixafortide CXCR4 chemokine receptor antagonist (class A) Stem-cell mobilization (myeloma) Sep 2023 41 Opvee nalmefene Opioid receptor antagonist (class A) Opioid-overdose reversal May 2023 113 Cardiometabolic and endocrine: the incretin era The largest cluster of GPCR approvals targets the incretin and glucagon receptors, all class B (secretin-family) GPCRs. Semaglutide (Wegovy) is a GLP-1 analogue that "acts as a GLP-1 receptor agonist that selectively binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor" 523 ; it entered the window as an obesity therapy in June 2021 375 . Tirzepatide is a dual "GIP receptor and GLP-1 receptor agonist" 460 , first approved as Mounjaro for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes in May 2022 459 354 and then as Zepbound for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight in November 2023 378 357 . The period closed with two notable additions. Orforglipron (Foundayo), approved April 2026 479 , is an orally administered agent whose labeling identifies "glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist activity" 480 , extending the incretin class beyond injectable peptides into a small-molecule oral format. Dasiglucagon (Zegalogue), approved March 2021 435 , works on the other side of glucose homeostasis: it is "a glucagon receptor agonist, which increases blood glucose concentration by activating hepatic glucagon receptors" 520 , indicated for severe hypoglycemia in patients with diabetes weighing at least 20 kg 520 . Neurology and headache: CGRP-receptor gepants Migraine has become a showcase for CGRP-receptor pharmacology, another class B GPCR. Atogepant (Qulipta) is a "calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist" 234 indicated for preventive treatment of migraine in adults 246 , approved September 2021 225 . Zavegepant (Zavzpret), the same mechanism 243 , was approved March 2023 231 as an intranasal spray for acute treatment of migraine with or without aura 248 . These small-molecule "gepants" sit alongside erenumab (Aimovig), the monoclonal antibody directed at the CGRP receptor itself rather than the ligand, which received a supplemental efficacy approval in this window 254 . The oral gepants rimegepant (Nurtec ODT) and ubrogepant (Ubrelvy) also received labeling and indication supplements during the period. Psychiatry and CNS: the first muscarinic-agonist antipsychotic Cobenfy (xanomeline/trospium), approved September 2024 36 , is the first antipsychotic to work through muscarinic rather than dopaminergic receptors. Its labeling attributes efficacy to xanomeline's "agonist activity at M1 and M4 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors in the central nervous system," with the co-formulated trospium acting as a peripheral muscarinic antagonist to limit cholinergic side effects 39 . It is indicated for schizophrenia in adults 39 . Both components engage class A muscarinic GPCRs, but as agonist and antagonist respectively. Sleep medicine: dual orexin-receptor antagonism Daridorexant (Quviviq), approved January 2022 332 , acts "through antagonism of orexin receptors," blocking orexin A and orexin B at the OX1R and OX2R receptors to suppress wake drive 336 . It is indicated for adults with insomnia characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or maintenance 340 . Orexin receptors are class A peptide GPCRs, and the dual-antagonist approach continues a mechanism established by earlier agents in the class. Immunology and neurology: sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators Two S1P receptor modulators, both acting on class A lipid-sensing GPCRs, were approved in the window. Ponesimod (Ponvory), approved March 2021 271 , is "a sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor 1 modulator" that blocks lymphocyte egress from lymph nodes 286 , indicated for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis 540 . Etrasimod (Velsipity), approved October 2023 259 , is a broader "S1P receptor modulator that binds with high affinity to S1P receptors 1, 4, and 5" 289 , indicated for moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults 289 . The two illustrate how receptor-subtype selectivity within one GPCR family is being tuned for different autoimmune indications. Women's health and menopause Relugolix, formulated with estradiol and norethindrone acetate as Myfembree, is a gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) receptor antagonist 536 , approved May 2021 199 for heavy menstrual bleeding associated with uterine fibroids and later for moderate-to-severe pain from endometriosis 214 . The GnRH receptor is a class A peptide GPCR. Distinct from hormonal suppression, fezolinetant (Veozah), approved May 2023 66 , is "a neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor antagonist that blocks neurokinin B binding on the KNDy neuron" to modulate the thermoregulatory center 530 , indicated for moderate-to-severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause 532 . Veozah was the first NK3-receptor antagonist approved for this indication. Rheumatology, nephrology, and dermatology Avacopan (Tavneos), approved October 2021 185 , is "a complement 5a receptor (C5aR) antagonist that inhibits the interaction between C5aR and the anaphylatoxin C5a," blocking C5a-mediated neutrophil activation 188 . It is an adjunctive treatment for severe active ANCA-associated vasculitis (granulomatosis with polyangiitis and microscopic polyangiitis) 188 , and was the first oral C5a-receptor antagonist. Difelikefalin (Korsuva), approved August 2021 90 , is "a kappa opioid receptor (KOR) agonist" 96 indicated for moderate-to-severe pruritus associated with chronic kidney disease in adults on hemodialysis 96 . As a peripherally restricted kappa-opioid agonist, it exploits a class A GPCR for an antipruritic rather than analgesic effect. Hepatology and critical care Terlipressin (Terlivaz), approved September 2022 75 , is "a synthetic vasopressin analogue with twice the selectivity for vasopressin V1 receptors versus V2 receptors" 533 , acting on class A vasopressin GPCRs to raise renal blood flow by reducing portal hypertension. It is indicated to improve kidney function in adults with hepatorenal syndrome and rapid reduction in kidney function 534 . Hematology and oncology support Motixafortide (Aphexda), approved September 2023 41 , is "an inhibitor of the C-X-C Motif Chemokine Receptor 4 (CXCR4)" that blocks binding of the ligand CXCL12/SDF-1 518 , disrupting stem-cell anchoring in the marrow. It is indicated in combination with filgrastim to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells for autologous transplantation in multiple myeloma 518 . CXCR4 is a class A chemokine GPCR, a target more familiar from HIV and oncology biology than from conventional small-molecule pharmacology. Addiction and emergency medicine Nalmefene (Opvee), approved May 2023 113 , "is an antagonist at opioid receptors" with a longer duration of action than naloxone 522 , indicated for emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose in patients aged 12 and older 522 . A nalmefene autoinjector (Zurnai) followed in August 2024 136 . Opioid receptors are class A GPCRs, and several buprenorphine reformulations acting as partial mu-opioid agonists (for example Brixadi, approved May 2023 100 ) also reached the market, alongside the meloxicam/rizatriptan combination Symbravo (January 2025 35 ), whose triptan component engages 5-HT1B/1D serotonin GPCRs. What the pattern shows Three observations stand out for regulatory and competitive-intelligence purposes. First, class B secretin-family receptors (GLP-1, GIP, glucagon, CGRP) drove both the highest-volume approvals and the most commercially significant ones, and the arrival of an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist signals a shift away from injectable peptides. Second, several approvals were deliberate first-in-class moves against long-validated but previously undrugged GPCRs, notably muscarinic agonism for schizophrenia, C5a-receptor antagonism for vasculitis, and NK3-receptor antagonism for menopause. Third, receptor-subtype selectivity, rather than a new target entirely, increasingly differentiates products within a class, as seen across the S1P modulators and the CGRP-receptor gepants. A reader tracking a specific indication or receptor subfamily would find it worth asking Rhizome directly for the underlying review documents, pivotal-trial endpoints, and any post-marketing or exclusivity details tied to each of these approvals.

title: 8 Top Sales engagement Platforms for Enterprise SDR Teams in 2026
summary: Explore the best sales engagement software for enterprise SDR teams. Compare Outreach, Salesloft, Trellus, Amplemarket, Apollo.io, Artisan, and Reply.io.
body_text: Enterprise sales teams have never had more technology available to support outbound prospecting. Each new year introduces another platform promising better personalization, smarter automation, higher reply rates, and more booked meetings. Yet many SDR organizations continue to spend hours every day researching prospects, updating CRMs, switching between applications, and manually managing follow ups. Industry research reflects both the opportunity and the growing interest in this category. MarketsandMarkets estimates the worldwide SDR market reached USD 4.12 billion in 2025 and projects it to grow to USD 15.01 billion by 2030. At the same time, several industry reports suggest annual sales based platform churn ranges between 50 and 70 percent , largely because many organizations expect complete automation while discovering that successful outbound still depends on thoughtful workflows, quality data, and well designed processes. The top sales engagement platforms for enterprise SDR teams have evolved far beyond simple sequencing tools. Modern platforms combine prospecting data, CRM synchronization, AI assisted writing, conversation intelligence, workflow automation, and analytics into a single workspace. Some focus on helping SDRs work more efficiently, while others aim to automate significant parts of the outbound motion. Finding the right platform depends on far more than feature comparisons. Enterprise buying decisions usually involve CRM compatibility, sales process maturity, implementation effort, reporting requirements, and the level of control sales leaders want over every stage of prospect engagement. If your team has been asking What are the best sales engagement platforms for enterprise SDR teams in 2026? , the answer depends on your outbound strategy, existing technology stack, and the amount of automation your organization is comfortable introducing into day to day prospecting. How We Evaluated These Sales Engagement Platforms Looking at marketing pages rarely tells the complete story. Almost every vendor promises higher productivity, AI powered personalization, automated outreach, and better conversion rates. Most enterprise sales leaders have learned that impressive demonstrations do not always translate into smoother workflows once hundreds of SDRs begin using the platform every day. Rather than comparing long feature checklists, we evaluated every solution from the perspective of an SDR manager, a RevOps leader, and a sales executive responsible for pipeline generation. We started with the sales motion Not every organization runs outbound in the same way. Some companies have hundreds of SDRs working entirely inside Salesforce. Others depend heavily on HubSpot, while growing organizations often prioritize simplicity over deep customization. Before evaluating software, we identified the environments each platform naturally supports. This included organizations running: Large Salesforce driven outbound organizations HubSpot centered revenue teams High volume prospecting operations Multi regional SDR organizations Growth stage companies consolidating multiple sales tools Smaller teams searching for a combined B2B prospecting and pipeline generation platform This made it easier to understand where every platform delivers the most value. We evaluated everyday SDR workflows The biggest differences rarely appear during product demonstrations. They appear on Monday morning when dozens of SDRs begin working through hundreds of prospects. We evaluated how each platform performs throughout an average working day. Areas we paid close attention to included: How SDRs prioritize daily activities Sequence creation and management Email personalization workflows Call execution Meeting scheduling Prospect research CRM updates Follow up automation Manager visibility into rep activity This provided a much clearer picture than comparing individual features. CRM alignment mattered just as much as automation Enterprise teams depend on accurate CRM data. Even the most advanced enterprise sales sequencing software creates unnecessary work if activities fail to synchronize correctly or reporting becomes unreliable. Every platform was evaluated for: Salesforce integration depth HubSpot synchronization Activity logging accuracy Forecast reporting compatibility Contact and opportunity updates Workflow automation reliability Organizations investing in SDR outreach automation software need automation that improves CRM quality rather than creating more administrative work. The Best Sales Engagement Platforms for Enterprise SDR Teams Enterprise SDR organizations often ask How do sales engagement platforms improve SDR productivity and meeting booking rates? The answer usually comes down to reducing repetitive work while helping reps spend more time speaking with qualified prospects. The best platforms automate administrative tasks , organize outreach, surface buying signals, and keep CRM records accurate without creating extra complexity. Below are our detailed recommendations, starting with two established enterprise leaders before moving into newer AI focused platforms. 1. Outreach Best for: Enterprise revenue organizations that need advanced outbound process management and highly structured prospect engagement. Outreach has remained one of the most recognizable names in enterprise sales engagement because it focuses heavily on execution discipline. Large sales organizations often struggle with inconsistent outreach. Different SDRs create different messaging, follow different cadences, forget follow ups, and update CRM records differently. Outreach brings those activities into a standardized workflow that managers can monitor and optimize. The platform combines multichannel sequencing, CRM synchronization, workflow automation, AI assisted messaging, reporting, and analytics inside one environment. For organizations managing hundreds of outbound representatives, consistency becomes just as valuable as automation. Its sequence builder remains one of the most mature products available for enterprise prospecting. Core capabilities Outreach includes a broad collection of features designed around structured outbound execution. Key capabilities include: Advanced multichannel sequence builder Email, phone, LinkedIn, and SMS engagement AI assisted email drafting Automatic reply detection Out of office handling CRM activity synchronization Built in meeting scheduling Call logging Messaging A/B testing Performance reporting across teams Workflow automation for repetitive prospecting tasks These capabilities help standardize outreach across large revenue organizations while giving managers visibility into every stage of outbound execution. Where Outreach performs well Enterprise organizations running mature outbound programs usually gain the most value. It performs particularly well for companies requiring strict process governance, consistent messaging, detailed reporting, and standardized sales cadences across multiple regions. Organizations looking for proven sales cadence tools for enterprise teams continue to place Outreach near the top of their evaluation lists because of its depth and operational maturity. Tradeoffs worth considering Outreach offers extensive customization, although implementation can require significant planning. Large deployments often involve RevOps teams, CRM administrators, and sales leadership working together before workflows become fully optimized. Smaller organizations may also find that many enterprise capabilities exceed their immediate requirements. CRM integration Salesforce remains its deepest integration, although HubSpot support continues to improve. Companies already operating mature CRM environments generally experience the smoothest implementation. Verdict Outreach continues to rank among the top sales engagement platforms for enterprise SDR teams because of its structured workflow design, enterprise reporting, and scalable outbound execution. 2. Salesloft Best for: Enterprise SDR and account development teams looking for structured sales execution, conversation visibility, and predictable outbound workflows. Salesloft has earned its place among the top sales engagement platforms for enterprise SDR teams because it focuses on helping sales organizations build repeatable outbound processes. Rather than relying on individual selling styles, the platform gives every representative a consistent framework for prospecting across email, phone calls, LinkedIn, and other engagement channels. For enterprise sales leaders, consistency often becomes one of the biggest contributors to pipeline growth. New hires ramp faster when everyone follows proven cadences. Managers can coach more effectively because every activity is tracked inside the same workflow. RevOps teams gain cleaner reporting because outreach data stays connected to CRM records throughout the sales cycle. The platform has gradually expanded beyond traditional sequencing, introducing AI assisted content creation, conversation intelligence, forecasting capabilities, and performance analytics. Despite these additions, its primary strength continues to be helping SDR teams execute organized outbound campaigns at scale. Companies comparing Outreach vs Salesloft: which sales engagement platform is better for enterprise SDRs? will often discover that both products solve similar problems while emphasizing slightly different workflow experiences. Outreach generally appeals to organizations looking for deeper workflow governance, while Salesloft often receives praise for its user friendly interface and coaching capabilities. Core capabilities Salesloft provides an extensive collection of features designed to help enterprise sales teams maintain consistent prospect engagement throughout every stage of the outbound process. Some of its most valuable capabilities include: Multi step cadence builder for email, phone calls, LinkedIn, and additional communication channels Intelligent task queues that organize daily outreach activities Automatic CRM activity logging AI assisted email drafting and messaging suggestions Conversation recording and transcription Coaching insights for managers Team performance dashboards Sequence reporting and engagement analytics Calendar scheduling Salesforce and HubSpot synchronization Together, these capabilities reduce manual administrative work while giving managers greater visibility into rep performance. Where Salesloft performs well Salesloft performs particularly well inside organizations that already have well defined outbound processes. Large SDR organizations benefit from the structured task management system because representatives always know which prospect should receive attention next. Managers gain access to detailed engagement reporting, making coaching sessions much more productive. It also fits organizations searching for mature enterprise sales sequencing software that balances automation with human involvement throughout the sales process. Companies looking for dependable SDR outreach automation software without introducing complete AI autonomy often place Salesloft high on their shortlist. Tradeoffs to consider Like many enterprise platforms, Salesloft delivers its best results after careful implementation. Cadences, reporting dashboards, CRM mappings, and workflow automation all require planning before teams experience the full value of the platform. Organizations expecting fully autonomous prospecting should also remember that Salesloft remains centered around empowering sales representatives rather than replacing them. AI assists the workflow, but SDRs continue making most engagement decisions. CRM integration Salesloft offers mature Salesforce integration alongside reliable HubSpot connectivity. Sales organizations with clean CRM data typically experience smooth synchronization across activities, contacts, meetings, and reporting dashboards. RevOps teams also benefit from strong visibility into outbound performance without requiring multiple reporting systems. Verdict Salesloft continues to rank among the best sales cadence tools for enterprise teams because it combines structured prospecting, strong CRM synchronization, coaching capabilities, and reporting into one polished platform. Enterprise organizations looking for repeatable outbound execution without unnecessary complexity will find plenty to like here. 3. Trellus Best for: Enterprise SDR teams that spend most of their day inside existing dialers and sales engagement platforms, and want AI to improve live selling rather than forcing everyone into an entirely new workflow. Most sales engagement platforms ask organizations to adopt another application. This AI-powered sales development platform takes a different direction. Rather than replacing the tools SDRs already rely on, Trellus layers AI directly into the outbound workflow your team already knows. Reps continue working inside familiar sales engagement software while gaining live coaching, conversation intelligence, prospect research, workflow automation, and AI assistance throughout the selling process. That philosophy makes adoption considerably easier for enterprise organizations. Sales representatives rarely enjoy learning another interface, especially when they already spend their day switching between CRM systems, dialers, sequencing software, LinkedIn, email, and internal communication tools. This platform reduces that friction by fitting naturally into the existing sales environment. For organizations searching for a modern B2B prospecting and pipeline generation platform , this creates a meaningful advantage. Sales leaders can enhance productivity without rebuilding their entire technology stack or forcing hundreds of SDRs through another lengthy onboarding process. One area where the platform particularly stands out is live sales execution. Most AI tools help before or after the conversation. They write emails, summarize meetings, or generate reports once the call has ended. Here, AI becomes part of the conversation itself. Representatives receive live coaching, objection handling guidance, conversation prompts, prospect intelligence, and workflow assistance while speaking with buyers. This keeps SDRs focused on the discussion rather than searching for information across multiple browser tabs. Core capabilities The platform brings together several capabilities designed around improving outbound conversations rather than simply automating repetitive tasks. Key capabilities include: Live AI sales coaching during active conversations Parallel dialing support through existing dialers AI generated prospect research before every conversation LinkedIn enrichment without interrupting workflow through our signature LinkedIn Superhuman feature! Real time objection handling suggestions AI practice calls for onboarding new SDRs Voicemail drop functionality Advanced call analytics Number health monitoring Rather than concentrating only on email sequencing, the platform places significant emphasis on helping SDRs perform better during the moments that directly influence pipeline creation. One of the biggest advantages is integration Enterprise sales organizations rarely depend on a single sales application. Most teams already have established workflows built around CRM platforms, dialers, sequencing software, conversation intelligence tools, and prospecting databases. Replacing all of those systems rarely makes financial or operational sense. One reason many enterprise teams evaluate Trellus is its extensive integration ecosystem. The platform works with many of the industry's most widely adopted outbound solutions, including: Outreach Salesloft Orum Apollo.io HubSpot Convoso Salesfinity Even more impressive is the company's willingness to build new integrations at no additional cost when customers use unsupported dialers. For enterprise organizations operating specialized sales technology stacks, this can significantly reduce implementation delays. Where it performs well This platform delivers the greatest value inside enterprise outbound teams where live conversations remain the primary source of pipeline generation. Organizations can continue using their preferred enterprise sales sequencing software while adding AI assistance across prospect research, coaching, dialing, and conversation management. It is particularly well suited for: Enterprise SDR organizations already invested in Outreach or Salesloft Teams using parallel dialers High volume cold calling organizations Companies onboarding new SDRs regularly Revenue teams looking to increase conversation quality rather than simply increasing activity volume Organizations searching for Best AI-powered sales engagement platforms for scaling enterprise SDR outreach Verdict Among today's top sales engagement platforms for enterprise SDR teams , Trellus fills a unique position. Rather than asking sales organizations to abandon proven workflows, it enhances them with AI where SDRs need help the most, before calls, during conversations, and immediately afterward. For enterprise teams committed to improving conversation quality, accelerating rep ramp time, and helping SDRs book more meetings without introducing another disconnected workflow, it deserves serious consideration. 4. Amplemarket Best for: Growth stage and enterprise sales teams looking for AI assisted prospecting, buying signals, sequencing, and deliverability tools inside one connected platform while keeping sales reps involved throughout the outbound process. Amplemarket has steadily expanded from a prospecting platform into a much broader outbound sales solution. Today, it combines contact discovery, sales engagement, buying signals, email deliverability, and AI assistance inside one environment, making it an attractive option for organizations trying to reduce the number of separate applications their SDR teams manage every day. One reason enterprise buyers continue evaluating Amplemarket is its balanced philosophy toward automation. Some AI platforms attempt to automate nearly every outbound activity from prospect discovery to campaign execution. Amplemarket takes a more collaborative route. AI handles research, surfaces opportunities, recommends actions, and prepares outbound campaigns, while sales representatives remain responsible for reviewing and approving communications before they reach prospects. For many organizations, this provides a comfortable middle ground. Sales leaders gain productivity improvements without giving up visibility into messaging quality or compliance requirements. Teams searching for an AI-powered sales development platform that supports outbound execution while keeping human oversight throughout the sales process will likely appreciate this operating model. Core capabilities Amplemarket brings together several outbound functions that many organizations traditionally purchase from separate vendors. Its feature set includes: AI agents supporting prospect research Buying signal detection Contact discovery and enrichment Multichannel sales engagement AI generated outbound sequences Personalized voicemail creation with AI voice cloning These capabilities allow SDRs to move from prospect discovery to outreach execution without switching between multiple applications throughout the day. Where Amplemarket performs well Amplemarket performs particularly well for organizations that want AI assistance across several stages of outbound prospecting while maintaining human review before campaigns launch. Enterprise teams often appreciate the combination of research automation, intent signals, deliverability monitoring, and multichannel engagement because these functions work together inside one platform. Companies building modern outbound programs also benefit from having prospect intelligence, engagement workflows, and deliverability tools connected rather than scattered across multiple systems. Organizations looking for a B2B prospecting and pipeline generation platform capable of supporting both prospect discovery and outreach execution frequently include Amplemarket during vendor evaluations. Tradeoffs to consider Amplemarket intentionally keeps sales representatives involved throughout outbound execution. For many organizations, this represents an advantage because managers retain oversight of messaging quality and campaign approvals. Companies searching for fully autonomous prospecting may find themselves performing more reviews than expected. AI assists with research, recommendations, and campaign preparation, although representatives still guide much of the final execution. Enterprise teams should also evaluate how much autonomy they want before deciding between collaborative AI platforms and products built around complete automation. CRM integration Amplemarket integrates with popular CRM platforms while supporting workflow synchronization across prospecting, engagement, and reporting. Organizations with established CRM processes generally experience the greatest value because prospect activity flows naturally into existing sales reporting. Verdict Amplemarket earns its position among the top sales engagement platforms for enterprise SDR teams because it combines prospecting, buying signals, engagement, and deliverability into a connected workflow. Sales organizations looking for AI assistance without handing complete control to automation will find the platform well suited to modern enterprise outbound programs. 5. Apollo.io Best for: Startups, scaling sales organizations, and SMBs looking for prospecting data, engagement tools, and outbound automation inside one affordable platform. Apollo has become one of the most recognizable names in outbound sales because it combines several categories of software that organizations traditionally purchased separately. Rather than subscribing to an external prospect database, another sequencing platform, another dialer, and another enrichment provider, many smaller sales teams begin with Apollo because it brings those capabilities together under one subscription. This makes onboarding considerably easier for growing companies that want to launch outbound prospecting without assembling a complicated sales technology stack from day one. Although Apollo continues expanding its AI capabilities, its primary value still comes from combining contact intelligence with outbound execution. Sales representatives can identify target accounts, build prospect lists, enrich company data, launch multichannel campaigns, and monitor engagement without constantly moving between applications. For organizations searching for practical SDR outreach automation software , Apollo offers one of the simplest entry points into outbound sales. Core capabilities Apollo combines prospecting intelligence with engagement capabilities designed for growing outbound teams. Key features include: Large contact and company database Advanced prospect filtering Company enrichment Buyer intent data Built in dialer Email sequencing This combination allows smaller organizations to build complete outbound programs without purchasing numerous standalone products. Where Apollo performs well Apollo performs particularly well for startups and fast growing sales organizations where budgets are limited but outbound activity continues increasing every month. Its integrated prospect database reduces the need for separate data providers, while sequencing and automation tools support daily SDR execution. Companies looking for an affordable AI-powered sales development platform frequently begin their evaluation with Apollo because of its generous free tier and accessible pricing structure. It also works well for organizations building outbound teams for the first time, since prospecting data and engagement capabilities already exist inside one platform. Tradeoffs to consider Although Apollo covers a wide range of outbound activities, enterprise organizations with highly specialized workflows may eventually outgrow some of its capabilities. Large SDR teams often require deeper workflow governance, more advanced reporting, sophisticated conversation intelligence, or broader automation than Apollo currently emphasizes. Organizations managing hundreds of sales representatives should evaluate how well the platform supports complex enterprise sales operations before committing long term. CRM integration Apollo integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and several popular sales applications. CRM synchronization works well for most growth stage organizations, while enterprise deployments may require additional workflow planning depending on reporting requirements. Verdict Apollo remains one of the most practical choices for organizations wanting prospecting data, engagement workflows, and automation inside one product. For companies searching for sales cadence tools for enterprise teams at the entry or mid market level, Apollo delivers considerable value without requiring multiple software subscriptions. 6. Artisan Best for: Organizations evaluating autonomous outbound prospecting with AI driven campaign execution and an integrated prospect database. Artisan has attracted considerable attention because of its ambitious vision for autonomous outbound sales development. Its AI business development representative, Ava, is designed to handle much of the prospecting workflow from identifying qualified contacts to launching campaigns and booking meetings. This places Artisan in a different category from traditional sales engagement software. Many established platforms concentrate on helping SDRs perform their work more efficiently. Artisan focuses on allowing AI to complete larger portions of outbound prospecting while human sales teams supervise campaign performance and make strategic decisions. Another factor that separates Artisan from many competitors is its built in contact database. Organizations evaluating the platform do not necessarily need to purchase separate prospecting data providers before launching outbound campaigns, simplifying implementation for many growing sales teams. Core capabilities Artisan provides several AI driven capabilities designed around autonomous outbound execution. Its feature set includes: Built in contact database Prospect enrichment Autonomous email campaigns AI meeting booking Campaign optimization Autopilot mode Copilot mode AI generated messaging Workflow analytics Outbound testing tools These features allow organizations to automate substantial portions of outbound prospecting while maintaining visibility into campaign performance. Where Artisan performs well Artisan performs best for companies interested in reducing manual prospecting activities through autonomous workflows. Organizations evaluating future focused outbound technology often appreciate having prospect discovery, enrichment, campaign creation, and AI execution inside one environment. Companies searching for Best AI-powered sales engagement platforms for scaling enterprise SDR outreach frequently include Artisan because of its emphasis on autonomous outbound execution rather than traditional sales engagement alone. Tradeoffs to consider Artisan currently places much of its emphasis on outbound email workflows. Organizations relying heavily on cold calling, live coaching, or multichannel engagement should evaluate how well the platform supports their preferred sales motion before making a purchasing decision. Enterprise buyers should also consider governance requirements, compliance processes, and approval workflows whenever autonomous messaging becomes part of customer communication. CRM integration The platform supports CRM synchronization alongside campaign reporting, allowing outbound activities to remain connected with pipeline management and sales reporting. Verdict Artisan represents one of the more ambitious entrants in the AI sales category. Organizations looking toward autonomous prospecting rather than traditional engagement workflows will likely find it one of the more interesting platforms currently available. 7. AiSDR Best for: Sales teams looking for intent driven outbound campaigns, transparent pricing, and AI supported prospecting without committing to a lengthy enterprise sales process. AiSDR has positioned itself around a simple idea. Sales teams should spend less time identifying who might be interested and more time speaking with prospects who already demonstrate buying intent. Rather than trying to become an all encompassing revenue platform, the software concentrates on helping organizations launch targeted outbound campaigns supported by AI insights and CRM connected workflows. This makes it appealing for companies that prefer a focused solution rather than a platform packed with features they may never use. One characteristic that stands out is pricing transparency. Many enterprise sales platforms require buyers to schedule demonstrations before receiving meaningful pricing information. AiSDR publishes pricing, allowing sales leaders to estimate costs much earlier in the evaluation process. For organizations building outbound programs with limited resources or carefully managed budgets, this removes a considerable amount of uncertainty. Companies searching for SDR outreach automation software with an emphasis on intent driven prospecting may find AiSDR worth evaluating alongside larger enterprise platforms. Core capabilities AiSDR focuses on practical outbound execution supported by AI rather than broad revenue management. Its core capabilities include: Intent based prospect targeting AI assisted outbound campaigns Campaign planning support Salesforce integration HubSpot integration AI generated GTM campaign ideas CRM connected workflows Activity reporting These features help sales teams identify accounts showing buying signals before launching outreach campaigns. Where AiSDR performs well AiSDR performs well for organizations running smaller, highly targeted outbound motions where quality matters more than sheer outreach volume. Companies that appreciate transparent pricing often include the platform early in their buying process because budgeting becomes much easier. Organizations beginning their search for an AI-powered sales development platform may also appreciate its focused product direction, especially if they are not looking for an extensive enterprise deployment. Tradeoffs to consider AiSDR concentrates on intent based outbound execution rather than covering every stage of the sales development lifecycle. Enterprise organizations requiring conversation intelligence, extensive workflow automation, advanced forecasting, multichannel orchestration, or complex governance should carefully compare its capabilities with larger enterprise platforms. Sales leaders should also evaluate channel coverage before making a decision, particularly if voice, LinkedIn engagement, or large scale outbound campaigns form a major part of their prospecting strategy. CRM integration The platform offers integration with both Salesforce and HubSpot, helping outbound activities remain connected with pipeline reporting and account management. Organizations already maintaining clean CRM records will generally experience the smoothest implementation. Verdict AiSDR offers an attractive option for organizations prioritizing intent driven outreach, transparent pricing, and straightforward implementation. While it may not provide the breadth of functionality found in larger enterprise platforms, it serves targeted outbound teams looking for focused AI support remarkably well. 8. Reply.io Best for: Sales teams looking for multichannel outreach, AI assisted communication, and affordable engagement software that supports growing outbound operations. Reply.io has been part of the sales engagement market for several years and continues to evolve alongside changing outbound sales strategies. The platform supports communication across email, phone calls, LinkedIn, SMS, and WhatsApp, allowing SDRs to reach prospects through multiple channels without relying on separate engagement tools. For growing sales organizations, this consolidated experience can simplify outbound execution considerably. Representatives manage sequences, conversations, follow ups, and campaign performance from one platform while AI assists with message creation and conversation handling. Another area where Reply.io continues receiving attention is mailbox management. Organizations running large email campaigns often struggle with deliverability and account limitations. Reply.io addresses part of this problem through unlimited mailbox support combined with built in email warmup functionality. Sales teams looking for a practical B2B prospecting and pipeline generation platform that combines multichannel engagement with AI assisted outreach frequently include Reply.io on their shortlist. Core capabilities Reply.io offers a broad collection of engagement features designed around modern outbound communication. Key capabilities include: Email sequencing LinkedIn automation Phone calls SMS messaging WhatsApp outreach AI powered email writing These capabilities help SDRs coordinate outreach across multiple communication channels while maintaining visibility into prospect engagement. Where Reply.io performs well Reply.io performs particularly well for organizations balancing growth with budget considerations. Sales teams gain multichannel outreach without purchasing numerous standalone engagement platforms, while AI assists with routine communication tasks that would otherwise consume valuable selling time. Organizations evaluating sales cadence tools for enterprise teams with broad communication coverage may find Reply.io especially attractive if email remains a significant part of their outbound strategy. Tradeoffs to consider Reply.io remains fundamentally a sales engagement platform enhanced with AI capabilities. Organizations searching for highly autonomous prospecting, advanced enterprise workflow governance, or comprehensive revenue orchestration may eventually require additional software alongside Reply.io. Enterprise buyers should also evaluate reporting depth, CRM customization, and operational scalability relative to their long term sales strategy. CRM integration Reply.io integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and several other CRM platforms, allowing outreach activity to remain synchronized with customer records and pipeline reporting. Verdict Reply.io continues to be one of the more balanced options available for organizations wanting multichannel engagement supported by AI. Its combination of communication channels, automation, and approachable pricing makes it a practical choice for growing outbound teams that value simplicity without sacrificing capability. How to Choose the Right Sales Engagement Platform Choosing among the top sales engagement platforms for enterprise SDR teams involves much more than comparing feature lists. Every sales organization has its own outbound strategy, CRM environment, reporting requirements, and operational priorities. A platform that performs exceptionally well inside one enterprise may create unnecessary complexity for another. If your team has been asking What features should enterprise SDR teams look for in a sales engagement platform? , these are the areas that deserve the closest attention. CRM integration should come first Sales engagement software becomes significantly more valuable when it works naturally with the systems your organization already depends on. Look for platforms that provide: Reliable Salesforce synchronization Strong HubSpot support Accurate activity logging Opportunity and contact updates Pipeline reporting alignment Poor CRM synchronization creates additional administrative work and reduces reporting accuracy across the revenue organization. Automation should support productivity AI continues improving rapidly, although complete automation does not always produce the best outcomes. Look for software that reduces repetitive administrative work while allowing sales representatives to remain engaged during relationship building and complex buying conversations. The most effective AI-powered sales development platform helps SDRs sell more effectively rather than simply generating more automated activity. Workflow adoption matters as much as features Even the most capable software produces limited value if sales representatives avoid using it. Enterprise organizations should evaluate: Ease of onboarding Learning curve User interface Daily workflow efficiency Manager visibility Reporting accessibility Higher adoption usually leads to cleaner CRM data, stronger reporting, and more consistent outbound execution. Integration with your existing technology stack Enterprise outbound rarely depends on one application. Many organizations already use conversation intelligence platforms, dialers, prospect databases, scheduling software, and CRM systems. Selecting software that connects naturally with existing tools reduces implementation effort while protecting previous technology investments. Frequently Asked Questions What are the best sales engagement platforms for enterprise SDR teams in 2026? Organizations evaluating enterprise sales engagement software frequently shortlist Outreach, Salesloft, Trellus, Amplemarket, Apollo.io, Artisan, AiSDR, and Reply.io. The right choice depends on your outbound strategy, CRM environment, preferred communication channels, and the amount of AI automation your sales organization wants to introduce. Outreach vs Salesloft: which sales engagement platform is better for enterprise SDRs? Both platforms serve enterprise sales organizations extremely well. Outreach places considerable emphasis on structured workflow management, governance, and process consistency across large SDR teams. Salesloft delivers a polished user experience with strong coaching capabilities and activity visibility. Many enterprise buyers evaluate both products before making a final decision. How do sales engagement platforms improve SDR productivity and meeting booking rates? Modern sales engagement platforms automate repetitive administrative work, organize daily outreach tasks, synchronize CRM activity, simplify follow ups, assist with personalization, and provide AI supported coaching. This allows SDRs to spend more time speaking with qualified prospects and less time managing manual workflows. What features should enterprise SDR teams look for in a sales engagement platform? Enterprise buyers should prioritize CRM integration, workflow automation, multichannel engagement, reporting, conversation intelligence, AI assistance, implementation quality, scalability, and compatibility with their existing sales technology stack. What is the difference between sales engagement software and an AI powered sales development platform? Traditional sales engagement software primarily helps SDRs organize outreach across email, phone, and social channels.

title: A developer's alternative to Intercom for product notifications
summary: Intercom is a support platform, and its API shows it: no push or SMS send endpoint. Why teams move product notifications to Courier, and how to migrate.
body_text: Intercom is a customer support platform. Courier is notification infrastructure. If you're using Intercom to send your product's transactional and marketing messages, you're using a help desk for a job its API was not built to do. If you're weighing an Intercom alternative right now, the timing isn't a coincidence. In May 2026, Intercom renamed itself Fin, after its AI support agent. A month later, Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire the company for about $3.6 billion, planning to fold that agent technology into Agentforce. The deal is signed, not closed, with Salesforce expecting it to complete in the final quarter of its fiscal 2027. The rename and the acquisition point the same direction, and it isn't lifecycle messaging. If you're deciding where your product's notifications will live for the next three years, one option is a support suite mid-acquisition whose roadmap is aimed at agent automation. That's a bet on someone else's priorities matching yours. Intercom vs Courier for product notifications What Intercom's API cannot do. No push or SMS send endpoint. Intercom's send endpoint accepts only in_app , email , and whatsapp . No way to reference a template you designed in the composer from code. No delivery status for email, push, or in-app messages. No API at all for Intercom Series, its campaign builder. What Courier does. Courier is notification infrastructure covering both transactional sends and marketing campaigns. One API call reaches email, SMS, push, in-app, and chat. Sends go through your own provider accounts, so your domains and sender reputation stay yours. Preferences are enforced at send time on every channel. Courier Journeys replaces Intercom Series for multi-step campaigns, adding batch, digest, and throttle nodes Series has no equivalent for. Courier Broadcasts handles one-off campaigns to an audience. The UI, the API, and an MCP server expose the same capabilities, so engineers, marketers, and coding agents work one platform. Cost. Courier charges $0.005 per message sent on any channel, with no per-seat or per-channel fees and 10,000 free sends per month. At published rates, sending 2,000 push notifications a month costs $223 on Intercom (one seat, the required $99 add-on, and metered usage) and $0 on Courier. Migration. Both transactional and marketing sends move to Courier. Do transactional first, since those calls are already API-driven, then rebuild Intercom Series as Courier Journeys. Intercom keeps the help desk. Courier's migration guide has the full concept mapping and a copy-pasteable prompt for running the work with a coding agent. Why Intercom isn't a fit Intercom hasn't announced any plan to sunset outbound messaging, and this post isn't claiming it has. The question is fit, and the clearest evidence isn't the strategy. It's the API. Everything below comes from Intercom's own published OpenAPI spec, version 2.16, read in August 2026. POST /messages is the only send endpoint, and this is its type enum: message_type: in_app | email | whatsapp No push. No SMS. The template field on the same call looks like a way out until you read its description: "The style of the outgoing message. Possible values plain or personal ." It's a style, not a reference, so content you built in the composer is unreachable from code and the body you send is HTML your backend assembled. from must be an admin, so every API send is attributed to a seat-holding human. And a flag called create_conversation_without_contact_reply exists because outbound sends are modeled as support conversations. Intercom is a support platform, and its send API is built like one. The consequence is that the only way to trigger a designed, multichannel message from your backend is indirect: post an event, and let a message you configured in the UI match against it. That path has documented ceilings. 120 active event names per workspace, and each event drives at most 50 live messages. No nested JSON. An order with line items doesn't fit. Deduplication on workspace, contact, event name, and timestamp to the second, so two legitimate identical sends in the same second collapse into one. Up to 24 hours before a new metadata field is usable in the composer. One event rule per message , and event-triggered messages aren't eligible for re-notification. The event returns 202 Accepted with an empty body. No message ID, and no delivery status endpoint for email, push, or in-app; the one that looks general is WhatsApp-only. So "did the password reset actually send?" has no programmatic answer. Why Courier fits Courier is notification infrastructure: transactional sends and marketing campaigns on one platform. That's the entire product rather than a module beside a help desk, and the difference shows up in the same place Intercom's focus does: what the API lets you do. What a product notification needs Intercom Courier Send on any channel from your backend in_app , email , whatsapp One call, every channel Reference content you designed Style only ( plain or personal ) Name a template Know whether it sent 202 , no ID, no status endpoint Message ID and delivery history Own your sending reputation Shared IPs, no outside provider Your provider accounts and IPs Consent across channels email and sms_message Every channel, topics enforced at send Roll-ups and frequency caps Precompute in your backend Digest, batch, throttle, send limits Version campaigns as code No Series API Journeys API Price that tracks sending Seats, add-on, per-channel metering $0.005 per send, flat Four of those need more than a table row. One send call covers every channel. You pass a recipient, a template, and data. Courier resolves which channels to use from the user's preferences and your routing rules, renders the content per channel, and returns an ID you can trace. Adding SMS to a notification that was email-only is a routing change, not a new integration. Your providers stay yours. Courier sends through your SendGrid, SES, Postmark, Twilio, or FCM accounts, on your domains and your IPs. Your deliverability is a thing you own and can fix, not a shared pool you're a tenant in. Configure more than one provider per channel and Courier fails over between them. Preferences are enforced, not advisory. Topics span every channel including push and in-app, and Courier checks them at send time rather than trusting each campaign to remember. Mark a topic required and receipts still reach someone who has opted out of marketing. A hosted preference page and embeddable components ship with it, so the unsubscribe experience exists on day one. Engineers, marketers, and agents use the same platform. Courier has full parity between the UI and the API, so nobody gets the degraded surface: Templates are built visually in Design Studio , one template holding email, SMS, push, in-app, and chat. Audiences are rule-built on profile attributes and update automatically as data changes. One-time sends run through Broadcasts : pick a template, pick an audience, send or schedule. Journeys replace Series for multi-step campaigns, with a visual editor over the same nodes engineers drive through the API, including experiments for testing message variants. An in-app inbox comes as a channel with drop-in components for React, iOS, Android, Flutter, and vanilla JS. Coding agents work the platform through the API and an MCP server , so an agent can build templates, wire journeys, and read delivery logs. Agent access is why these migrations move faster than they used to. The mechanical work, reading a campaign definition and creating its equivalent, is exactly what an agent is good at, and Courier exposes every capability it needs to do it. What changes for transactional sends Transactional is where a support platform's assumptions hurt most, because the requirements are strict. Intercom's documentation says dedicated IP addresses aren't available and all email goes over shared IPs, with no option to send through your own provider, so your password resets share reputation with other companies' campaigns. Event-driven email usually sends in seconds but can take up to 30 minutes under load. When activity restrictions trigger, email only reaches contacts seen or engaged within the last 180 days, which is exactly the wrong constraint for a dormant user asking for a password reset. And Subscription Types accept only email or sms_message , so there's no push or in-app consent model. Courier changes all four, because you send through your own provider accounts rather than a shared pool. Your domains, your reputation, your dedicated IP if you have one, and no engagement-recency rule standing between a dormant user and their login code. What changes for marketing sends Series does real work, and rebuilding it takes real effort. Three things change shape. Roll-ups move into the platform. Intercom has no digest primitive, so "one summary instead of nine notifications" gets precomputed in your backend before you fire the triggering event. Courier has batch and digest nodes that collapse many events into one message inside the journey. Frequency capping stops being per-message. Intercom caps occurrences on each message individually, so nothing coordinates across campaigns. Courier's send limits cap volume globally, per user, per topic, or per tenant, holding across every journey and broadcast at once. Localization stops being copy-paste. Intercom's documented approach is to duplicate the message per language and target each copy with an audience rule on the contact's language. Eight locales, eight messages to keep in sync. Courier keeps locales on one template: set locale on the profile or the send, and the right version renders. AI Translations generates those locale versions from the template you already wrote, so adding a language is a step rather than a project. What Courier costs compared to Intercom Comparing Intercom and Courier isn't license against license. Intercom prices notifications like a support tool: per seat, plus a $99 add-on for the journey builder and transactional sending, plus per-message metering on the channels notifications actually use. Courier's pricing page states its model in one line: "based on notifications sent, not team size or channels." Intercom Courier Pricing basis Per seat, plus usage per channel Per message sent, volume pricing at scale Published rates cover Up to 2,000 messages/month Any volume Entry price $29 to $132 per seat per month Free tier (10,000 sends/month), then $0.005 per message Push $0.06 to $0.07 after a 500/month allowance $0.005 Email From $0.045, tiered $0.005 SMS $0.06 to $0.09 per segment, carrier included $0.005 plus your own carrier rate Provider choice Intercom's shared IPs only Your own provider accounts Delivery status API WhatsApp only Every message Here's the smallest complete comparison, built only from what both companies publish. Send 2,000 push notifications a month, which is the top of Intercom's published rate card: Intercom Courier Plan minimum 1 Essential seat, $29 Free Developer tier, $0 Journey builder Proactive Support Plus, $99 Included Transactional sending Same $99 add-on Included 2,000 push messages 500 included, then $0.07 and $0.06 by tier: $95 Inside the 10,000 free sends Monthly total $223 $0 Courier stays free to 10,000 sends a month, five times that volume, before you pay anything. After that it's $0.005 a send on every channel, with volume pricing available as you scale. Above 2,000 messages Intercom's rates aren't published, so a like-for-like number at real volume doesn't exist. Courier publishes its rate up front instead, and once you're sending more than 100,000 messages a month, come talk to us about volume pricing. Intercom discounts heavily too, especially for startups. The difference is where the conversation starts: with a published number, or without one. When Intercom is still the right call Support is the job. If what you need is a help desk, an AI agent that resolves tickets, a help center, and a shared inbox, Intercom is a strong product and this post isn't an argument against it. Most teams migrating notifications to Courier keep Intercom for support. Your outbound is onboarding UI, not messages. Product tours, tooltips, checklists, and banners are in-product guidance. Courier doesn't replace those. In-app banners are on our roadmap; the rest belong in Intercom or a product-adoption tool. Your volume is tiny and your channels are email-only. If you send a few hundred messages a month, all email, entirely to recently active users, the ceilings above are theoretical and the add-on may be cheaper than a migration. How do you migrate off Intercom? Transactional first. Those sends are already API-driven, they carry the most risk if they break, and shared IPs and a 30-minute delay ceiling serve them least well. The order that works: inventory every live outbound message and Series, split it into transactional, marketing, and in-product guidance, then find the events in your code that exist only to trigger a message. Those become direct send calls, which is usually a small diff. Connect your providers, sync profiles, rebuild the highest-volume templates, and run both systems in parallel until the output matches. Map Subscription Types to preference topics and import opt-outs before any marketing send. Then rebuild Series as journeys, one at a time. Push tokens are the one item you can't rush. Intercom collects them through its SDK, so they live inside Intercom rather than in your data. Start registering tokens with Courier from your app while Intercom is still live and let coverage build across a release cycle or two. The full concept mapping, the documented constraints with citations, and a copy-pasteable prompt for running the work with a coding agent are in our guide to migrating from Intercom to Courier . Frequently asked questions Is Courier a replacement for Intercom? Not for support. Courier replaces the notification layer: transactional sends, campaigns, journeys, templates, preferences, and an in-app inbox across email, SMS, push, in-app, and chat. Intercom's help desk, Messenger, tickets, Help Center, and Fin have no Courier equivalent, and most teams keep them. The split that works is Intercom for conversations with your support team, Courier for what your product sends. Can I send a push notification through the Intercom API? No. POST /messages accepts only in_app , email , and whatsapp . To send a push from your backend you post an event to POST /events and rely on a message you configured in the UI matching against it, which returns 202 Accepted with no message ID and no delivery status endpoint to check afterward. What replaces Intercom Series in Courier? Journeys . Entry rules become triggers (API invoke, inbound webhook, Segment event, or audience membership), waits become delay nodes, rules branches become branch nodes, and messages become send nodes. Journeys add batch, digest, throttle, and fetch-data nodes that Series has no equivalent for, and unlike Series they can be built through the API. Can Courier handle marketing campaigns, or only transactional messages? Courier handles both. Courier Journeys is a visual campaign builder for multi-step lifecycle and onboarding sequences, and it replaces Intercom Series directly. Broadcasts handles one-off sends to an audience. Marketers get a UI for templates, audiences, broadcasts, and journey editing, and engineers get the same capabilities through the API. Journeys also add batch, digest, and throttle nodes that Series has no equivalent for. How much does Intercom cost for notifications? Intercom pricing for notifications has three layers. Intercom charges per seat, $29 to $132 per seat per month, plus $99 a month for the Proactive Support Plus add-on that gates Series and transactional messaging, plus per-message usage: $0.06 to $0.07 for push and other "Messages Sent" channels after a 500/month allowance, from $0.045 for bulk email, and $0.06 to $0.09 per SMS segment. Those published tiers only run to 2,000 messages a month; above that, pricing is negotiated. Courier charges a flat $0.005 per message on any channel at any volume, with 10,000 free per month. On SMS the two aren't directly comparable: Intercom's per-segment rate includes the carrier cost, while Courier's $0.005 sits on top of your own carrier bill. Does Intercom support transactional email? Yes, with four caveats. It requires the Proactive Support Plus add-on. All email goes over Intercom's shared IPs, with no dedicated IP option and no way to use your own provider. Intercom documents that event-driven email can be delayed up to 30 minutes under load. And activity-based restrictions can limit sending to contacts active within the last 180 days, which is exactly the wrong constraint for a password reset. What happens to my Intercom contacts and custom attributes? Contacts become Courier user profiles keyed by user_id , with the contact's external_id as the identifier and channel addresses carried across. Custom attributes become profile attributes, and because profiles accept nested JSON, structures you had to flatten for Intercom can keep their shape. Segments become audiences that recalculate as attributes change. Is Intercom being shut down after the Salesforce acquisition? No, and nothing reported suggests outbound messaging is being discontinued. Focus is the more useful question. Intercom pivoted to AI in 2023, renamed itself after its AI support agent in May 2026, and Salesforce's stated rationale for the $3.6 billion acquisition is folding that agent technology into Agentforce. The deal is signed, not closed, with Salesforce expecting it to complete in the final quarter of its fiscal 2027. The API shows where the investment has already gone. Intercom's help desk surface is deep and well maintained: conversations, tickets, macros, teams, help center, voice. Outbound has one send endpoint that covers three message types, no push or SMS endpoint, no delivery status, and no campaign API at all. Notifications and lifecycle messaging are not a focus area for a company that has committed itself entirely to AI customer support. Choosing Intercom to send your product's messages for the next three years means betting that changes under new ownership. Where to start If you are evaluating an Intercom alternative, start with the guide to migrating from Intercom to Courier , or create a free account and send your first message on the free tier before committing to anything.

title: Paysafe Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
body_text: Aug 13, 2026 London, UK – August 13, 2026 – Paysafe Limited (NYSE: PSFE) today announced financial results for the second quarter of 2026. Second Quarter 2026 Summary (compared to Q2 2025, unless noted) Revenue of $447.4m increased 4%; net loss of $58.9m or ($1.13) per diluted share Adjusted net income of $23.1m or $0.43 per diluted share Adjusted EBITDA of $102.8m decreased 2% Executed the refinancing of the company's revolver and term loans "We delivered second quarter results in line with our expectations, with revenue growing 4% in the quarter and 7% in the first half, driven by strong traction across our priority markets and products," said Bruce Lowthers, CEO of Paysafe. "Our investments in innovation, marketing, and data commercialization are continuing to generate returns, with our Product Vitality Index remaining on track toward our mid-term target of 20%. We also took important steps to strengthen our financial foundation by refinancing the majority of our capital structure and resolving a legacy legal matter. As we enter the second half of the year, we remain focused on execution, deleveraging, and building on the durable growth opportunities across our global network of consumers and merchants." Second Quarter of 2026 Summary of Consolidated Results Three Months Ended Six Months Ended June 30, June 30, ($ in thousands) (unaudited) 2026 2025 2026 2025 Revenue $ 447,444 $ 428,218 $ 890,167 $ 829,218 Gross Profit (excluding depreciation and amortization) $ 243,769 $ 238,038 $ 493,818 $ 464,857 Net loss $ (58,949) $ (50,132) $ (95,401) $ (69,604) Net loss per share - Diluted $ (1.13) $ (0.85) $ (1.84) $ (1.17) Adjusted EBITDA $ 102,807 $ 104,997 $ 202,045 $ 200,167 Adjusted net income $ 23,143 $ 27,631 $ 44,180 $ 48,544 Adjusted net income per share - Diluted $ 0.43 $ 0.46 $ 0.84 $ 0.80 For the second quarter of 2026, Paysafe reported revenue of $447.4 million, an increase of 4% on both a reported and organic basis, compared to $428.2 million for the second quarter of 2025, reflecting 3% growth from Digital Wallets and 6% growth from Merchant Solutions. In Digital Wallets, continued momentum and active user growth from Latin America and PaysafeWallet in Europe more than offset the expected impact from rest of world markets where Paysafe is not actively marketing, as well as temporary grow-over effects in certain sub-verticals, including social casino and cryptocurrency trading. In Merchant Solutions, growth was driven by strong iGaming volumes in North America and was further supported by the company's commercialization of data through licensing agreements. Net loss for the second quarter was $58.9 million, or ($1.13) per diluted share, compared to $50.1 million, or ($0.85) per diluted share, in the prior year period, including an increase in restructuring and other costs of $18.6 million, primarily related to legal costs. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $19.3 million, reflecting an increase in share-based compensation of $11.4 million, mainly due to performance awards and one-time share awards granted to a majority of employees in the first quarter of 2026, as well as an increase in marketing investment of $7.1 million. These impacts were partly offset by a $22.5 million decrease in income tax expense. Adjusted net income for the second quarter decreased to $23.1 million, compared to $27.6 million in the prior year period. Adjusted EPS for the second quarter was $0.43, compared to $0.46 in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter decreased 2% to $102.8 million, compared to $105.0 million in the prior year period as revenue growth was partially offset by an increase in selling, general and administrative expenses (excluding share-based compensation). Movement in foreign exchange rates was favorable to second quarter revenue and Adjusted EBITDA by $5.0 million and $1.7 million, respectively. Second quarter operating cash flow decreased to $25.3 million, compared to $39.6 million in the prior year period, reflecting higher operating expenses as described above, excluding non-cash items, offset partially by lower working capital outflows. Unlevered free cash flow was $44.8 million, compared to $53.9 million in the prior year period. Compared to December 31, 2025, total debt decreased by $106.3 million, mainly reflecting net repayments of $79.1 million, as well as fluctuations in the EUR/USD exchange rate, which decreased total debt by $33.9 million. Refinancing Transaction On August 12, 2026, Paysafe refinanced portions of its existing Term Loan Facility (USD) and Term Loan Facility (EUR), with settlement of funds due on August 17, 2026. The refinancing transaction includes a new $650.9 million Term Loan Facility and a new €478.4 million Term Loan Facility, each maturing in June 2030. In addition, the company refinanced its existing revolving credit facility with a new senior secured $372.5 million revolving credit facility maturing in August 2031. More information can be found in the 6-K filed by the company today and in the supplemental earnings presentation, which is available on the investor relations section of the Paysafe website. "We are very pleased to have completed this transaction, which underscores our prudent approach to managing the balance sheet and liquidity," said John Crawford, CFO of Paysafe. "The refinancing extends our debt maturity profile, refinances a significant portion of our capital structure, and upsizes our revolver, while supporting our priorities to invest in the business and reduce leverage for the benefit of both lenders and shareholders.” Full Year 2026 Financial Guidance The company updated its full year 2026 financial guidance for Adjusted EPS to account for the refinancing transaction and associated change in interest expense. With 30 years of expertise in payment technology, Paysafe helps businesses and consumers lift every experience through seamless, secure payment solutions, including card payments, digital wallets such as Skrill, eCash solutions like PaysafeCard, and a suite of local payment methods. With approximately 2,800 employees across 12 countries and annualized transactional volume of $167 billion in 2025, Paysafe connects people and businesses worldwide through innovative digital payment experiences.
